title: audit-picks
universal_lens: The pick lifecycle is modeled as a finite directed graph $G=(V,E)$, where vertices represent discrete states and edges denote valid transitions. The audit enforces topological constraints: ensuring strong connectivity to terminal nodes (win/loss/push/void) and eliminating cycles or unreachable subgraphs that violate conservation of state integrity.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the state machine acts as a strict conformal filter for Bayesian updates. Observables (game outcomes) trigger transitions; illegal mutations are treated as distributional shifts. We map unreachable states to high-Kullback-Leibler divergence regions, flagging them as structural model failures requiring immediate recalibration of the underlying probability measures.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the state machine dictates permissible agent actions under concurrency. Race conditions during simultaneous grade/settle operations manifest as non-deterministic edge traversals. The engine maps these to Petri nets, enforcing mutual exclusion locks on state mutations to guarantee causal consistency across distributed event streams.

primitives.assumptions: Every initiated pick must eventually resolve to a member of the terminal set Omega; no infinite loops are permitted in the active state space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity arises if an edge case (e.g., abrupt game cancellation) creates an orphaned state lacking a defined path to Omega, freezing capital allocation.

layer2.mapping: Maps to spectral graph theory; orphaned states correspond to disconnected components in the transition graph with zero out-degree to terminal nodes.
layer2.telemetry: Count of unresolved picks exceeding maximum expected duration thresholds.

The provided excerpts define a rigorous software engineering audit translated into a mathematical framework for Galaxy Sports Intelligence. The core operator is the 'Pick Lifecycle State Machine', which we formalize as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) or Finite State Automaton (FSA). The primary objective is to ensure that every node (pick) initialized in the system possesses a valid, unbroken path to one of the designated terminal nodes: win, loss, push, or void. 

Mathematically, this involves constructing an adjacency matrix representing permissible transitions. The audit process utilizes version control telemetry (git diff, git log) to reverse-engineer this matrix from the codebase. A critical failure mode identified is the existence of 'orphaned' or 'unreachable' states—nodes with zero out-degree that do not belong to the terminal set. In a probabilistic context, these represent leaked probability mass, violating the axiom that the sum of probabilities over all terminal outcomes must equal unity.

Furthermore, the excerpts highlight 'race conditions on concurrent grade/settle'. This introduces a temporal dimension to the state machine. If the grading (evaluating outcome) and settling (updating financial state) processes occur simultaneously without proper mutex locking or transactional isolation, the system may traverse an illegal edge, mutating a pick's state outside the defined FSA. This duality between static graph topology (illegal transitions) and dynamic concurrency (race conditions) forms the bedrock of our sovereign primitives. The GSI layer treats these violations as high-entropy anomalies, while the GSE layer models them as breakdowns in causal consistency, necessitating strict serialization of state mutations.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agent not as a human bettor, but as an adversarial concurrency tester or a malicious actor attempting to exploit race conditions. Their goal is to force the system into an undefined state by triggering simultaneous grade/settle events, thereby bypassing the state machine's validation logic to manipulate the final resolution of a pick before it reaches a terminal state.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto is issued if the static analysis of the state machine reveals any non-terminal state lacking a guaranteed path to resolution, or if dynamic profiling shows that the grade/settle operations lack strict mutual exclusion. Leakage occurs if financial mutations are permitted outside the explicit transition function, breaking the isomorphism between the logical state graph and the physical database transactions.
